newsitem.title: USA: GM CEO says GM needs different from Ford's.
newsitem.headline: GM CEO says GM needs different from Ford's.

text.p: General Motors Corp Chairman Jack Smith declined to comment Tuesday on what impact the United Auto Workers tentative pact with Ford Motor Co could have on GM, but he made a point of saying GM's needs are different from Ford's.

"Obviously, General Motors is a different company than Ford," Smith told reporters at a press conference to announce that the city of Detroit is moving into headquarters buildings that GM plans to vacate.
Smith said he will refrain from commenting on the Ford-UAW deal, announced Monday, because the details are not known.
Ford and the UAW reached a tentative deal on a new three-year labor pact that calls for Ford to maintain employment for 95 percent of its UAW hourly workforce.

Some analysts have speculated that could be bad news for GM, which is seeking to lower its workforce. In the past, the UAW has used its agreement with one of the Big Three as a pattern for similar agreements at the remaining two.
Smith said he is not sure if the UAW's contract with Ford would be beneficial to GM.

"I believe (UAW President) Steve Yokich has shown real statesmanship in the negotiation process this year," Smith said. "He said that he believes it's a contract that will work for all three companies, and we'll just have to see how that works out."

Richard Wagoner, president of GM's North American Operations, speaking at a different function, told reporters that GM would like to be the next of the Big Three automakers on which the union focuses.
"We always want to be next," Wagoner told reporters before an address at the Ritz-Carlton Hotel in Dearborn, Mich.
Yokich said Monday the UAW has not decided if it will start the final stage of bargaining with GM or Chrysler Corp next.

Wagoner said discussions between GM and union bargainers are moving along, adding that some issues have been settled while others have not been. He declined to characterize which issues are still outstanding.
